record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For MAX-CUT, where the input is an n-vertex graph G = (V, E) and the task is to find a subset X of V that maximizes the number of edges between X and V - X, design a faster exact algorithm than the O*(2^(omega n/3))-time approach based on reducing to 3-clique in an auxiliary graph, where omega is the matrix multiplication exponent and O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Design a faster exact algorithm for MAX-CUT.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the exponent of square matrix multiplication, i.e., the infimum of real numbers $c$ such that two $n \times n$ matrices over a ring can be multiplied using $O(n^c)$ ring operations. Use $O^*(\cdot)$ to suppress factors polynomial in the input size.

The MAX-CUT problem is defined as follows: given an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$ on $n = |V|$ vertices, find a subset $X \subseteq V$ that maximizes the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $X$, i.e., the size of the cut $|\{\{u,v\} \in E : |\{u,v\} \cap X| = 1\}|$.

A known exact algorithm solves MAX-CUT in time $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$ by reducing the problem to finding a maximum-weight triangle in an auxiliary graph of $2^{n/3}$ vertices and then applying fast matrix multiplication.

Problem: Design an exact algorithm for MAX-CUT on general $n$-vertex graphs whose worst-case running time is asymptotically faster than $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$ bound due to Williams (via reduction to max-weight triangle) remains the best known worst-case running time for exact MAX-CUT on general $n$-vertex graphs. Subsequent work has focused on sparse graphs, special graph classes (e.g., split graphs), counting versions, or polynomial-space variants, but no improvement on the general-graph exponent has been reported. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Maximum cut - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Williams' algorithm runs in O*(2^{ωn/3}) time, the fastest known for general graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$ bound is still cited as the fastest known exact algorithm for MAX-CUT on general graphs.

status_evidence.title: Exact Algorithms for MaxCut on Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For special classes such as split graphs there is an O*(1.42^n) time algorithm; whether a polynomial-space algorithm for MaxCut faster than O*(2^n) exists is open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works address restricted classes and polynomial-space variants, indicating no improvement on the general-graph exponent.
